公开阅读反馈 暂缓自动推荐: https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Identifying+post-necking+hardening+of+anisotropic+materials+from+a+single+tensile+test+ori&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.ijsolstr.2026.114397%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Reliable structural analyses require material models calibrated using experimental data, typically obtained from tensile tests on cylindrical specimens. When anisotropic behavior is involved, the interpretation of such tests becomes significantly more complex, as the specimen cross-sections evolve into non-axisymmetric and generally unknown shapes. The present study proposes a simplified framework for identifying the strain-hardening behavior of anisotropic materials in testing scenarios characterized by limited optical access and availability of only cylindrical specimens with a fixed orientation. The proposed approach employs synchronized recordings from two camera views and a 360° scan of fractured specimens. Under the assumption of elliptical cross-sections, this data is used to reconstruct the evolution of the three-dimensional specimen shape during the test. Based on this reconstruction, the area-based true stress–strain curve is determined and subsequently corrected into an analytical estimate of the equivalent stress–strain response in the post-necking regime. This curve is further refined through a hybrid experimental–numerical procedure involving a single correction iteration and relying on isotropic hardening and simplified assumptions regarding the anisotropic yield behavior and its parameters. Owing to its simplicity, the approach provides a first-order estimate of the strain-hardening law, but it is particularly suited for experimental campaigns in which testing along multiple loading directions is unfeasible. The method offers reduced experimental cost, adaptability to demanding testing environments, and efficient identification. Its applicability is demonstrated through an experimental campaign conducted on an ITER grade CuCrZr alloy and over a wide temperature range up to 580 °C, complementing the currently available hardening data relevant to EU-DEMO divertor applications. item.title: Shear-sensitive failure prediction for ultra-thin steel sheets: A combined necking and fracture framework incorporating through-thickness anisotropy
item.description: 库内相似论文：Application of Necking and Uncoupled Ductile Fracture-Based Models to Estimate Formability of Thin Sheets Using Anisotropic Yield Theories（相似度 0.756） 复杂应力状态与屈服准则: 可作为屈服面形式、压力/Lode 依赖与试样构型设计的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对应力状态覆盖范围、是否含负三轴度、加载路径是否比例 摘要片段: A hybrid experimental strategy was used … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 延性断裂准则: 可作为断裂轨迹形式与起裂判据的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Shear-sensitive+failure+prediction+for+ultra-thin+steel+sheets%3A+A+combined+necking+and+fra&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1177%2F10567895261500976%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Failure prediction of ultra-thin deep drawing steel under shear-related forming paths requires the combined assessment of localized necking and ductile fracture. In this study, 0.3 mm BDCK ultra-thin deep drawing steel was characterized by uniaxial tensile and Nakajima tests. The material exhibited weak in-plane anisotropy but pronounced through-thickness anisotropy, with an average r -value of 1.720. A hybrid experimental strategy was used to determine the necking forming limit curve and fracture forming limit curve from near-pure shear to balanced biaxial tension. The results show that localized necking and fracture act as competing failure limits, indicating that both limits should be evaluated within a unified framework. For necking prediction, an updated modified maximum force criterion model accounting for through-thickness anisotropy and shear-sensitive strain-path evolution was employed. For fracture prediction, the Hu-DFC criterion incorporating through-thickness anisotropy was adopted after comparison with DF2012. The framework was applied to a box-shaped deep drawing process. The predicted localized necking and fracture displacements showed relative errors of approximately 8.8% and 7.0%, respectively. The predicted critical region agreed with the experimental fracture location near the die shoulder radius. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Characterization+of+Dynamic+Deformation+Behavior+and+Constitutive+Model+of+TB9+Titanium+Al&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.3390%2Fcoatings16101237%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 In the cryogenic-ultrasonic elliptical vibration cutting (UEVC) of TB9 titanium alloy, high-strain-rate deformation occurs, and its cryogenic dynamic deformation behavior and constitutive model are crucial for analyzing the cutting process. Static stress–strain curves were obtained using an electronic universal testing machine, while dynamic stress–strain curves under different temperatures and strain rates were measured using a split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) apparatus. Based on the Johnson–Cook (J-C) constitutive model, a modified J-C (M-J-C) constitutive model was developed by adjusting the strain rate sensitivity factor and temperature exponent. The results showed that TB9 exhibited certain strain rate sensitivity and temperature sensitivity. At low temperatures, the flow stress of TB9 titanium alloy first increased and then decreased with strain rate; as the temperature decreased, the flow stress of the material gradually increased. Compared to the original J-C model, the M-J-C curves showed closer descriptive agreement with the reported plastic stress–strain responses within the fitted domain. The proposed model was subsequently implemented in a finite element model of cryogenic-UEVC, and its predictive performance was evaluated through corresponding cutting experiments. Under machining parameter set No. 1, the experimentally measured surface residual-stress magnitude was approximately 355 MPa, whereas the original J-C and M-J-C models predicted 411 MPa and 391 MPa, respectively, reducing the prediction error from 15.7% to 9.8%. For parameter sets Nos. 2–4, the prediction errors of the M-J-C model were lower than those of the original J-C model by 9.4%, 4.2%, and 6.4%, respectively. These results demonstrate that incorporating the coupled effects of strain rate and temperature improves the description of the dynamic deformation behavior of TB9 titanium alloy and enhances the predictive capability of finite element simulations for cryogenic-UEVC. item.title: Abaqus implementation of the phase-field approach to fracture
item.description: 库内相似论文：A fully explicit phase-field model for multi-physical fracture and its efficient implementation in ABAQUS（相似度 0.721） 用户子程序与数值实现: 可作为显式积分算法、正则化方案与子程序实现细节的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Abaqus+implementation+of+the+phase-field+approach+to+fracture&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.48550%2Farxiv.2610.24820%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 In this paper, we introduce an Abaqus user-subroutine implementation of the phase-field model of fracture initiated by Kumar, Francfort, and Lopez-Pamies (\emph{J. Mech. Phys. Solids} 112, 523--551, 2018). The implementation is presented for the basic case of isotropic linear elastic brittle materials with a Drucker-Prager strength surface. The material inputs are therefore the Young's modulus $E$, the Poisson's ratio $ν$, the uniaxial tensile strength $\sts$, the uniaxial compressive strength $\scs$, and the fracture toughness $G_c$. The mathematical correspondence between the heat equation and the evolution equation for the phase field $v(\bfX,t)$ is exploited through a UMAT subroutine, wherein the driving force $c_{\texttt{e}}(\bfX,t)$ --- accounting for the material strength surface --- in the phase-field model plays the role of a heat source. To ensure that the equations for the displacement field $\bfu(\bfX,t)$ and the phase field $v(\bfX,t)$ are solved in a staggered manner --- a solution strategy that, as opposed to monolithic approaches, reliably yields the correct physical solution --- we make use of a combination of UEXTERNALDB, UAMP, MPC, and URDFIL subroutines. Within this approach, the MPC and URDFIL subroutines are additionally utilized to enforce the required bounding and irreversibility inequalities on $v(\bfX,t)$ via a primal-dual active set approach. The capabilities and robustness of the proposed implementation are demonstrated by simulating the ``Nine Circles of Elastic Brittle Fracture'' on a silicate glass --- a set of tests that span the entire range of well-settled experimental knowledge on fracture nucleation and propagation. These simulations also serve to illustrate the deployment of the code using several native Abaqus finite elements, including the simplicial elements CPS3, CAX3, and C3D4. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Characterization+of+anisotropy+in+sheet+metals+using+digital+image+correlation&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.58845%2Fjstt.utt.2026.en.6.5.112-126%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22calibration%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 This study develops and applies an in-house two-dimensional digital image correlation (2D-DIC) system to investigate the anisotropic behavior of sheet metals under uniaxial tensile loading. Two materials, SUS304 stainless steel and DP1200 dual-phase steel, were examined. Tensile specimens were prepared along three orientations with respect to the rolling direction: rolling direction (RD), diagonal direction (DD), and transverse direction (TD), and the tests were performed in accordance with ISO 6892-1. The DIC method provided full-field displacement and strain measurements on the specimen surface, enabling the determination of stress–strain curves, Lankford coefficients, normalized yield stresses, and yield surface characteristics. The results show that SUS304 exhibits high ductility, strong strain hardening capacity, and more pronounced planar anisotropy than DP1200. In contrast, DP1200 shows higher tensile strength but lower elongation, and its Lankford coefficients and normalized yield stresses are closer to isotropic behavior. Comparison of the yield criteria indicates that Hill48 represents the anisotropic response more accurately than the von Mises criterion. Hill48-R agrees better with the experimental Lankford coefficients, whereas Hill48-S more accurately describes the normalized yield stresses. Continuum Damage Mechanics (CDM) traditionally represents material degradation through scalar or tensorial damage variables that describe the progressive loss of material integrity. Although tensorial damage measures, including fourth-rank damage tensors, have previously appeared in the literature, the novel contribution of the present work is not the introduction of the fourth-rank damage tensor itself. Instead, this article develops a unified hierarchy of classical, updated, and generalized damage formulations and systematically extends this hierarchy from scalar damage to second-rank and fourth-rank tensor representations. The classical formulation provides the established reference model, whereas the updated damage relation and the generalized damage relation introduced here are new formulations. The generalized formulation further contains both the classical and updated models as exact special cases through appropriate choices of its governing parameters. This construction therefore establishes a single mathematical framework in which three distinct levels of damage degradation—classical, updated, and generalized—are related systematically rather than treated as independent constitutive models. The proposed hierarchy is developed first for scalar damage and subsequently extended to second-rank and fourth-rank damage tensors, thereby permitting a progressive transition from isotropic degradation to directional anisotropic damage and, ultimately, to general coupling among stress modes. Particular emphasis is placed on the new updated and generalized degradation equations, their admissibility requirements, limiting behavior, spectral representation, and recovery of the classical theory. The fourth-rank formulation is embedded within a thermodynamically consistent framework that includes a damage-driving force, damage criterion, evolution law, and conditions for non-negative dissipation. A 6 × 6 matrix representation provides a direct route toward computational implementation, while spectral decomposition establishes practical conditions for invertibility and numerical admissibility. The resulting framework therefore provides a unified extension of CDM in which the principal original contribution is the classical–updated–generalized hierarchy of degradation laws, with the newly proposed updated and generalized relations providing additional flexibility for representing nonlinear material degradation. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Microstructural+Design%2C+Processing%2C+and+Dynamic+Deformation+of+Advanced+High-Strength+Stee&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.58830%2Fozgur.pub1505.c6032%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Advanced high-strength steels (AHSS) are increasingly considered for energy-absorbing applications because they can combine high load-carrying capacity with reduced structural mass. Their suitability, however, cannot be assessed solely from nominal yield or tensile strength, since deformation and fracture behavior are strongly controlled by microstructure, processing history, and strain-rate sensitivity. This chapter examines the relationships among processing, microstructure, deformation mechanisms, formability, and dynamic fracture in high-strength steels used for energy absorption. Particular attention is given to ferrite, martensite, bainitic constituents, and retained austenite, together with the effects of phase-strength mismatch, strain partitioning, global and local ductility, and retained-austenite stability. The principal thermomechanical processing routes used to produce HSLA, DP, TRIP, CP/FB, Q&P, TBF, medium-Mn, and press-hardened steels are reviewed with emphasis on their microstructural objectives. Manufacturing-induced effects, including pre-strain, local thinning, cut-edge damage, and bending, are also considered because they modify the deformation capacity available during subsequent loading. High-strain-rate behavior is discussed in terms of strain-rate hardening, adiabatic heating, phase transformation, and dynamic fracture. Finally, emerging strategies involving retained-austenite engineering, high-ductility press-hardened steels, and spatially tailored microstructures are evaluated. The overall assessment shows that optimum energy-absorbing performance requires a balanced combination of strength, strain-hardening capacity, local ductility, fracture resistance, and controlled microstructural heterogeneity rather than maximum strength alone. item.title: Disseny i simulació numèrica d'estructures d'absorció d'energia per a l'aterratge mitjançant el mètode dels elements finits
item.description: 库内相似论文：A comparative study of the hexahedral elements in LS-DYNA for crashworthiness simulation（相似度 0.694） 损伤演化与孔洞机制: 可作为损伤累积形式与孔洞机制建模的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对损伤变量定义、是否与塑性耦合、单元尺寸依赖是否处理 摘要片段: In addition, a damage evolution model … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 用户子程序与数值实现: 可作为显式积分算法、正则化方案与子程序实现细节的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对单元类型与尺寸、耗散能、稳定性与网格收敛性 摘要片段: The simulations are performed using Abaqus/Explicit. … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 [EN] The development of reusable space vehicles requires landing systems capable of absorbing the energy generated during impact and reducing the loads transmitted to the vehicle. This Bachelor’s Thesis develops a numerical model based on the finite element method to analyse the behaviour of an aluminium hexagonal cell subjected to axial compression, as a simplified representation of a honeycomb structure used in the energy-absorbing components of rocket landing legs. The simulations are performed using Abaqus/Explicit. The model consists of a rigid base, an impactor and a cell manufactured from EN AW-7108 T6 aluminium alloy. Initially, an elastic model is used to verify that the analysis has been configured correctly. Subsequently, the plastic behaviour of the material and the ductile, shear and MSFLD damage initiation criteria are incorporated. In addition, a damage evolution model and an element deletion criterion are included in the constitutive model. Starting from a reference configuration, a parametric study is conducted in which the cell wall thickness, the impactor mass and the initial impact velocity are varied independently. The different configurations are compared by analysing the stress, strain and displacement fields, the force-displacement response, the impactor kinematics, the energy balance and the activation of the damage criteria. The results show that the cell absorbs part of the kinetic energy through plastic deformation and the progressive formation of folds. Increasing the wall thickness increases the contact forces and reduces crushing, whereas decreasing the thickness reduces the initial force peak at the expense of greater deformation. Similarly, increasing the impactor mass or velocity increases the amount of energy that the structure must absorb and makes it more difficult to bring the impactor to a complete stop. The methodology developed enables different configurations to be compared and provides a useful tool for the future optimisation of this type of structure, although the results will need to be validated through experimental testing. ABSTRACT Fatigue resistance in metals is fundamentally constrained by a long‐standing dilemma: the strain hardening required to suppress deformation localization is typically achieved through the accumulation of dislocations and other defects that ultimately promote fatigue damage. Whether cyclic plasticity can be sustained without progressive defect storage remains an unresolved question. Here we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome through the introduction of amorphous nanoparticles into a crystalline metal matrix. We uncover a cyclic deformation regime characterized by sustained resistance to strain localization yet minimal net defect accumulation over prolonged loading. During cyclic deformation, the amorphous nanoparticles function as efficient dislocation sinks, continuously mitigating defect accumulation in the metallic matrix, while their elastic deformation via reversible shear transformations provides apparent strain hardening of the overall material. These synergistic mechanisms effectively preserve the microstructural integrity of both the metallic matrix and the amorphous nanoparticles over millions of loading cycles, leading to a fatigue life of more than 10 5 cycles at a fatigue ratio of 0.95, and a ratcheting rate one to three orders of magnitude lower than all known metals and alloys. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Relative+Density+Effects+on+Deformation+Mechanisms+and+Failure+Modes+in+Gyroid+Lattices&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.mtla.2026.102929%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22lpbf_tc4%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices such as the sheet-based gyroid are promising for lightweight structural and energy absorbing applications, but the deformation and damage processes governing post-yield failure and their dependence on relative density remain insufficiently resolved. This study investigates the evolutionary states of laser powder bed fusion Ti-6Al-4V gyroid lattice unit cells under compression and how these states are related to the global structural response of the lattice, building on prior work establishing the relative density dependence of the modulus and yield stress of such gyroids. Uniaxial compression tests on unit cells and periodic gyroid lattices spanning 3-60% relative density, interrupted at intermediate global strains, are combined with in situ stereoscopic digital image correlation, X-ray micro-computed tomography, and high-resolution finite element calculations to resolve strain localization and damage evolution. A gradual transition in failure mode is identified: unit cell hinging precedes rapid structural collapse at lower relative densities and ductile fracture failure dominates at higher relative densities. These findings provide a basis for understanding failure in metal gyroid lattices under compression and support geometry-based strategies for improving structural performance and fracture resistance. Crashworthiness design of high-strength steel structures requires the coordinated consideration of material behavior, structural geometry, joining, fracture, and manufacturing history. Although higher-strength steels offer significant opportunities for lightweighting through thickness reduction, increased nominal strength does not automatically improve crash performance because changes in stiffness, local buckling, collapse mode, and fracture sensitivity may alter the structural response. This chapter examines the crashworthiness of high-strength steel energy-absorbing structures from a component- and structural-level perspective. Fundamental performance measures, including energy absorption, specific energy absorption, mean crushing force, peak crushing force, and crush force efficiency, are introduced together with progressive and unstable collapse modes. The coupled effects of material strength, wall thickness, section geometry, and collapse initiators are then evaluated. Particular attention is given to local ductility, manufacturing-induced pre-strain, cut-edge damage, and fracture because these factors can interrupt progressive deformation before the available crushing stroke is fully utilized. The role of resistance spot welding, laser welding, mechanical fastening, and other joining methods in load transfer and collapse continuity is also discussed. Numerical crashworthiness assessment is addressed through constitutive modelling, strain-rate dependence, stress-state-dependent fracture, joint representation, contact, mesh sensitivity, forming-to-crash transfer, and experimental validation. Automotive, rail, and heavy-transport applications are considered using a function-based material-selection approach. Finally, emerging strategies based on tailored properties, integrated material–geometry optimization, and manufacturing-aware crash simulation are discussed. The overall assessment demonstrates that effective crashworthiness depends on controlled deformation and reliable load-path continuity rather than maximum material strength alone. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+multi-constitutive+four-dimensional+lattice+spring+model+for+high-velocity+penetration+o&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.ijrmms.2026.106756%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22impact_validation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 High-velocity penetration of kinetic projectiles into brittle targets (rock and concrete) involves coupled large deformation, fragmentation, and damage evolution. To simulate these coupled responses within a unified framework, a multi-constitutive four-dimensional lattice spring model (4D-LSM) is developed. Johnson-Holmquist-Beissel (JHB) model is adopted to describe the pressure-dependent strength, damage and fragmentation of rock and concrete. A modified Johnson-Cook (MJC) model is proposed for metallic projectiles by incorporating damage-dependent strength and shear-stiffness degradation, residual strength-based thermal softening, and incremental damage evolution. The resulting coupled framework, termed MJC-JHB-4DLSM, integrates the two constitutive models through a unified explicit stress-update procedure. The MJC formulation is independently validated against Taylor impact tests, reproducing the axial shortening, radial expansion, and progressive failure of metallic rods under high strain-rate loading. The coupled framework is further assessed through hypervelocity penetration of long rods into concrete and granite targets. Typical crater–tunnel and crater-dominated failure modes, projectile erosion, and penetration-regime transitions are successfully reproduced. The predicted penetration depth and residual projectile response show reasonable agreement with experimental observations. Simulations of oblique penetration into multilayer spaced concrete targets further capture the progressive accumulation of projectile attitude perturbation and trajectory deviation. The proposed framework provides a unified continuous-discontinuous approach for analysing high-velocity penetration into rock-like targets, with potential applications to the design and safety assessment of underground protective structures. Phase-field cohesive zone model (Wu 2017) with Drucker-Prager plasticity in effective stress, for compressive and tensile failure of cementitious materials, implemented as an Abaqus/Standard UMAT and HETVAL. The phase field is solved as the temperature degree of freedom (Navidtehrani et al. 2021), so only a UMAT and a HETVAL are needed. This code extends the open UMAT + HETVAL code of Navidtehrani, Betegón and Martínez-Pañeda; with the first nine material constants it gives the same results as that code. The archive contains the Fortran source (PFCZM-WuZhou_EN.for), a user manual with a worked example, technical notes, one representative Abaqus input file for each example of the companion paper, and the data behind its figures and tables (CSV). Tested with Abaqus/Standard 2017 and Intel Visual Fortran 17.0 on Windows 10. Companion paper: C.G. Dengiz, A phase-field cohesive zone model with Drucker-Prager plasticity in Abaqus/Standard: implementation, solution schemes and verification for compressive failure of cementitious materials (submitted to Finite Elements in Analysis and Design). Published: 2026-10-15T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research) 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

ABSTRACT This study experimentally and numerically investigates fatigue damage in additively manufactured 316L stainless steel produced by selective laser melting using the powder bed fusion–laser beam process. More than 100 specimens were tested under tensile and strain‐controlled fatigue loading to evaluate the effects of surface condition, hot isostatic pressing (HIP), and build orientation. Machining provides the greatest improvement in fatigue performance by removing sub‐surface defects, while HIP provides additional benefits through reduced porosity. Vertically built specimens exhibit approximately 40% longer fatigue life than diagonal and horizontal specimens because elongated grains aligned with the build direction enhance ductility and stabilize crack propagation. A unified continuum damage mechanics‐based constitutive model predicts cyclic softening and fatigue life across low‐ and high‐cycle regimes. Fatigue anisotropy is represented by an orientation‐dependent fatigue ductility coefficient, while remaining parameters are orientation‐independent. The model accurately reproduces cyclic hysteresis loops and fatigue life to failure. item.title: Application of an extended void growth model with strain hardening and void shape evolution to ductile fracture under axisymmetric tension
item.description: 经典文献补漏 库内相似论文：Ductile fracture by void growth to coalescence（相似度 0.896） 被相关论文引用：Decoding Fracture Surface Morphology to Understand Dynamic Fracture Energy of Austenitic Stainless Steels [https://doi.org/10.1007/s11665-026-15165-3] 与《Micromechanically-motivated phenomenological Hosford–Coulomb model for predicting ductile fracture initiation at low stress triaxialities》共享 10 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.167 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W196283644, https://openalex.org/W1976393181, https://openalex.org/W1985778844, https://openalex.org/W2010178746, https://openalex.org/W2016303309
